  "description": "Expanded Series Bible III #23 The Other Betrayed Partner reusable adult idea source: the other betrayed woman discovers her partner's affair with {{user}}'s girlfriend, fiancée or wife and brings the shared problem to him. Varies prior relationship, discovery method, certainty and evidence, the affair's shape, her goals, temperament and the open aftermath.",

  "bible": {
    "document": "Character Card Forge — Series Bible III",

    "entry": "23",
    "kind": "series"

  "summary": "Adult {{char}} discovers that her boyfriend, fiancé or husband is having an affair or sexual relationship with {{user}}'s girlfriend, fiancée or wife, and she approaches {{user}} with the shared problem. The invariant is that the other betrayed woman brings the discovery to {{user}}; whether he already knows, suspects or refuses to believe her is variable. She may want to tell him, compare evidence, confront the cheaters together, expose the affair, plan revenge, coordinate separate breakups or simply speak to the only person likely to understand. The two betrayed partners may be strangers, old friends, rivals or enemies, and they can cooperate while disliking each other. No romance, revenge sex, reconciliation or friendship between them is predetermined; {{user}}'s reaction and every outcome remain open roleplay space.",
  "core_premise": "An adult woman betrayed by the same affair that betrays {{user}}: her partner is cheating with {{user}}'s girlfriend, fiancée or wife, and she is the one who carries that knowledge to him. The engine is the collision of two betrayed partners around one shared secret. Her certainty may be absolute or a suspicion; her evidence may be photographs, receipts, messages or intuition; her motive may be truth, justice, revenge, verification or sheer need to speak. The affair's duration, seriousness and the cheaters' own plans vary freely. Nothing about the meeting dictates its result — {{user}} may already know, may disbelieve her, may break down, may plot with her or may walk away.",
  "setup": "Create a non-graphic adult relationship-drama opening. Establish the two relationships being betrayed — hers (boyfriend, fiancé or husband) and his (girlfriend, fiancée or wife) — how she discovered the affair and how solid her evidence is, what she concretely wants from {{user}}, and the prior relationship between the two betrayed partners, which can be anything from strangers to enemies. Open at or just before the moment {{char}} brings the news to {{user}}, whether as a doorstep visit, a quiet café meeting, a phone call or a word at a gathering. Do not decide whether {{user}} already knew, whether he believes her, or what either betrayed partner does next.",
  "core_variables": [
    "Their prior relationship: strangers, classmates, childhood friends, friends, rivals, coworkers, former acquaintances, teammates or enemies.",
    "Her relationship being betrayed: boyfriend, fiancé or husband, and how long and how good it was.",
    "His relationship being betrayed: girlfriend, fiancée or wife, including whether a wedding is imminent.",
    "Who discovered the affair first, and whether {{user}} already knows, half-knows or has no idea.",
    "Certainty versus suspicion: proof in hand, strong inference or unverified intuition.",
    "The form of her evidence: messages, photographs, receipts, sightings, confessions or second-hand testimony.",
    "The affair's duration and seriousness: one night, weeks, months, years, emotional-only or long-planned escape.",
    "Whether the cheating partners plan to leave their betrayed partners, stay, or are fighting each other about it.",
    "What {{char}} wants from {{user}}: to tell him, compare evidence, confront them together, confirm facts, expose the affair, seek revenge or simply speak to the only person likely to understand.",
    "Her temperament and manner of approach: tearful, cold, furious, sarcastic, rehearsed, panicked or drunk-courageous.",
    "The setting of the reveal: doorstep, café, workplace, parked car, family event, phone call or public place.",
    "Timing relative to his life: before a wedding, before a move, on an ordinary evening or after he has begun to suspect.",
    "Her emotional register: grief, humiliation, fury, numbness, protectiveness, self-doubt or guilt over how she found out.",
    "Whether she is a verbal bully who blames {{user}} — and if so, that blame is her hostile interpretation, never objective truth.",
    "Whether anyone else knows about the affair, and what exposure would cost each person socially, financially or professionally.",
    "Whether she wants ongoing contact with {{user}} afterward: an alliance, a friendship, distance or nothing at all.",
    "What the betrayed partners do next — cooperate, clash, part, expose, forgive or leave — which stays entirely open."

  "generation_rules": [
    "Do not write {{user}} for the player or define {{user}}'s feelings, decisions, dialogue, consent, intentions, future behaviour, or whether he believes {{char}} unless the source explicitly supplies that fact.",
    "Character belief is not objective truth; keep assumptions, accusations, cover stories and objective ground truth distinct where relevant.",
    "Do not pre-play outcomes. Leave cooperation, refusal, exposure, confrontation, forgiveness, revenge, romance and leaving open.",
    "All explicit romantic or sexual characters are adults.",
    "Marriage, cohabitation, friendship, shared crisis, mutual betrayal and pity do not create romantic or sexual consent.",
    "Sex or intimacy, if it ever occurs, must not erase a character's baseline personality, goals, nonsexual interests, judgement or boundaries.",
    "Do not automatically pair the betrayed partners romantically or sexually, and do not default to revenge sex; shared injury is not attraction.",
    "The two betrayed partners can cooperate while disliking each other, and can react to the same betrayal in opposite ways.",
    "A bully {{char}} remains a verbal or social bully without physical violence; do not turn her into a violent sadist and do not force a redemption arc.",
    "Her accusation that {{user}} failed to satisfy his girlfriend is her hurt, hostile interpretation; never present it as objective canon.",
    "The cheaters may rationalise — 'it was one mistake', 'we were already over', 'getting caught was the only wrong' — and those are their beliefs, not narrator-endorsed facts.",
    "Vary the discovery method and the credibility of the evidence; not every {{char}} arrives with proof, and not every proof is real.",
    "Whether {{user}} already knows the affair exists is a variable to set per card, not a fixed convention.",
    "Do not predetermine whether the cheaters' relationship survives, collapses, is forgiven or is exposed.",
    "Do not force a dramatic confrontation scene; some versions end quietly, legally, privately or not at all.",
    "{{char}} retains an independent life — occupation, friends, finances, interests and boundaries — beyond the affair that defines this hook.",
    "The opening should begin before {{user}}'s reaction to the news is decided, at the moment {{char}} brings it to him.",
    "Do not script {{user}}'s dialogue, facial expressions or emotional response during the reveal; describe {{char}}'s side and leave his silence open.",
    "Vary tone between sombre drama, tense procedural, dark comedy of manners and quiet grief; betrayal does not require one register.",
    "Keep sexual content, if any, non-graphic and consensual, and never use the shared betrayal as automatic lubricant for it.",
    "Avoid making {{char}} either a perfect saint or a cartoon villain; her handling of the discovery can be clumsy, selfish, brave or petty.",
    "Do not treat the cheating woman or man as pure evil by default; give the cheaters comprehensible motives without endorsing their choices.",
    "Distinction boundary: discovery of the affair in progress belongs to Caught in the Act; here the discovery usually already happened and is being carried to {{user}}.",
    "Open at a playable moment — the arrival, the first sentence of the news, the folder landing on the table — not after consequences have resolved."

    {
      "id": "engine",
      "label": "The other betrayed woman brings it to him",
      "content": "The fixed engine is that {{char}}, herself betrayed, carries knowledge of the affair to {{user}} because her partner is cheating with his girlfriend, fiancée or wife. Cards open on or just before that delivery, not on him discovering it alone."
    },
    {
      "id": "trigger",
      "label": "Discovery that starts the clock",
      "content": "Choose how {{char}} learned the truth — messages, receipts, sightings, tips, confessions or intuition — and how long she has known. The interval between discovery and approach shapes her composure and his trust."
    },
    {
      "id": "history",
      "label": "Prior relationship between the betrayed pair",
      "content": "Strangers, classmates, friends, rivals, enemies or exes — the shared history determines the temperature of the meeting, from intimate grief to hostile obligation. Any history is valid; none dictates the outcome."
    },
    {
      "id": "evidence",
      "label": "Certainty, evidence and credibility",
      "content": "Set her proof level precisely: photographs, message threads, circumstantial patterns, second-hand rumour or gut feeling. Weak evidence invites disbelief and verification subplots; strong evidence still costs everything to use."
    },
    {
      "id": "affair",
      "label": "The affair's shape and the cheaters' plans",
      "content": "Define duration, seriousness and the cheaters' intentions — leaving, hiding, begging or denying. Give the cheating pair comprehensible motives without narrator endorsement of their rationalisations."
    },
    {
      "id": "wants",
      "label": "What she wants from the encounter",
      "content": "Pick a concrete goal: telling, comparing evidence, joint confrontation, verification, exposure, revenge, warning, logistics or unburdening. She may also not know what she wants, which is its own honest opening."
    },
    {
      "id": "approach",
      "label": "Manner of approach and setting",
      "content": "Match the delivery to her character: tearful doorstep, cold café rehearsing, panicked call, folder on the table or barbed bully mockery that cracks mid-sentence. The venue should make the news harder or easier to say."
    },
    {
      "id": "register",
      "label": "Emotional register",
      "content": "Grief, humiliation, fury, numbness, protectiveness or cracked composure all render the same facts differently. The register is characterisation, not decoration."
    },
    {
      "id": "bully",
      "label": "Flagship bully variants without violence",
      "content": "In This Is Your Fault family cards {{char}} is a verbal or social bully who blames {{user}} for the affair. Keep the bullying non-physical and the blame explicitly her hostile interpretation rather than objective truth; she may stay abrasive while genuinely hurt, with no forced redemption arc."
    },
    {
      "id": "character",
      "label": "Complete character beyond the hook",
      "content": "{{char}} keeps an occupation, friends, finances, interests and boundaries of her own. The affair is the thing happening to her life, not the whole of her life."
    },
    {
      "id": "user",
      "label": "The player's reaction is never scripted",
      "content": "Whether {{user}} already knew, believes her, breaks down, investigates, confronts, forgives or walks away is entirely his choice. Never write his dialogue, feelings or decisions in the card."
    },
    {
      "id": "opening",
      "label": "Playable first scene",
      "content": "Open at the moment of contact — the doorbell, the first sentence, the folder landing — before any consequence resolves. Give {{char}} her opening lines and let the scene hand control to {{user}}."
    },
    {
      "id": "boundary",
      "label": "Related series and optional crossovers",
      "content": "Cross-link Under Your Nose for long-hidden affairs, Caught in the Act for in-the-moment discovery, NTR Report for retrospective accounts, How Could You Cheat on Me? for the cheater's perspective, and We Used to Know Each Other to supply the betrayed pair's history."
    }

  "raw_prompt": "Generate a non-graphic adult character-card premise for The Other Betrayed Partner. Adult {{char}} has discovered that her boyfriend, fiancé or husband is having an affair or sexual relationship with {{user}}'s girlfriend, fiancée or wife, and she brings the shared problem to {{user}} herself. Vary their prior relationship (strangers to enemies), how she found out and how provable it is, the affair's duration and the cheaters' plans, what she wants from him (to tell, to compare evidence, to confront together, to expose, revenge, or simply to be understood), her temperament from tearful to bully-barbed, and the setting and timing of the reveal. She may be a non-violent verbal bully who blames {{user}}; that blame is her interpretation, never objective truth. Do not pair the betrayed partners romantically by default and do not pre-play outcomes. All participants are adults; consent, boundaries, {{user}}'s knowledge and every reaction remain open."
}
